ridge-tech.note: Ridge's own PDF for this vintage, read as text.

ridge-ava.name: Ridge Vineyards, Santa Cruz Mountains AVA
ridge-ava.about: Monte Bello and the AVA, not vintage specific

claims.claim: 84% Cabernet Sauvignon and 16% Merlot.
claims.quote: 84% CABERNET SAUVIGNON, 16% MERLOT

claims.claim: 13.3% alcohol.
claims.quote: 13.3% ALCOHOL BY VOLUME
claims.note: Some merchants list 14%. The tech sheet is used.

claims.claim: 100% air-dried American oak barrels, half new and half one year old.
claims.quote: 100% air-dried American oak barrels; (50% new and 50% one-year-old)

claims.claim: Nineteen months in barrel.
claims.quote: Nineteen months in barrel

claims.claim: Destemmed and sorted. Fermented as whole berries on native yeast.
claims.quote: 100% whole berries fermented on the native yeasts

claims.claim: Full malolactic fermentation on naturally occurring bacteria. Minimal sulfur.
claims.quote: full malolactic on the naturally occurring bacteria; minimum effective sulfur

claims.claim: pH 3.51 and total acidity 7.0 g/L.
Bottled in July 2023.
claims.quote: bottled 7/23

claims.claim: The fruit comes from Ridge's Monte Bello Vineyard, mainly the Klein Ranch lots.
claims.quote: a selection of lots primarily from Monte Bello's Klein Ranch

claims.claim: The Estate Cabernet parcels cover 38.5 acres and gave 70.2 tons, or 2.1 tons per acre.
claims.quote: 70.2 tons from 38.5 acres

claims.claim: Fractured limestone soils under decomposing Franciscan greenstone mixed with clay and loam.
claims.quote: Fractured limestone soils overlaid with decomposing Franciscan green stone mixed with clay/loam

claims.claim: Elevation runs from 1,300 to 2,670 feet.
claims.quote: Elevation: 1300’ to 2670’

claims.claim: The oldest vines were planted in 1949. Later plantings run from 1968 to 2013.
claims.quote: Oldest 1949; further plantings in 1968/9, 1972, 1982

claims.claim: Vines are head-trained and cane-pruned on vertical trellis. They are not irrigated once established.
claims.quote: Non-irrigated. (New vines receive drip irrigation until fully established)

claims.claim: Monte Bello's first blocks were planted in 1886 and the first vintage was 1892.
claims.quote: In 1886 the first blocks of the Monte Bello vineyard were planted

claims.claim: Younger Monte Bello blocks made a more approachable wine, first sold as Santa Cruz Mountains in 1978. It became Ridge Estate Cabernet Sauvignon with the 2008 vintage.
claims.quote: With the 2008 vintage the name of this stylistically distinct wine became the Ridge Estate Cabernet Sauvignon

claims.claim: A dry winter with 14 inches of rain, 30% of normal, stressed the vines and cut yields.
claims.quote: Rainfall: 14” (30% of normal)

claims.claim: Bloom was in early May. A heat wave in early September sped up the harvest, which ran 21 to 24 September at 24.4 Brix on average.
claims.quote: Harvest Dates: 21-24 September

claims.claim: For the first time in over 50 years, Ridge finished the Monte Bello harvest before Lytton Springs.
claims.quote: For the first time in our 50+ year history we finished our Monte Bello harvest before Lytton Springs

claims.claim: The warm summer concentrated flavor and called for care in fermentation so tannin was not over-extracted.
claims.quote: required extra attention during fermentation not to over extract tannin

claims.claim: Estate Cabernet tends to mature somewhat earlier than Monte Bello. Ridge calls it a pure, mountain Cabernet.
claims.quote: This pure, mountain cabernet is best cellared for two to three years

claims.claim: Ridge says to cellar it two to three years, then it improves over the following ten to fifteen. That points to about 2025 to 2038.
claims.quote: best cellared for two to three years and will improve over the following ten to fifteen
claims.note: Counted from the July 2023 bottling. The end year is our arithmetic on Ridge's words.

claims.claim: CellarTracker window is 2027 to 2038.
claims.note: From the brief. Matches the end of Ridge's range.

claims.claim: Ridge describes its approach as minimal intervention: hand-harvested estate fruit, native yeast, minimal sulfur.
claims.quote: In keeping with our philosophy of minimal intervention, this is the sum of our actions.

claims.claim: Taste dots: dry; medium-full body from 13.3% alcohol; fresh acidity from TA 7.0 g/L and pH 3.51; firm tannin from mountain Cabernet and Ridge's note on careful extraction.
Flavors read from mountain Cabernet's typical profile and 50% new American oak: black currant, black cherry, cedar, graphite, herbs, vanilla. No 2021 tasting note was found.
Pairings are the classic Cabernet Sauvignon pairings: lamb, grilled steak, aged cheddar, mushroom dishes.
claims.note: Wine Folly's Cabernet Sauvignon guide, the house pairing source for Cabernet.

claims.claim: Sheet window 2025 to 2038, from Ridge's cellar-two-to-three-years-then-ten-to-fifteen advice.

conflicts: Alcohol: Ridge says 13.3%, some merchants list 14%. Ridge used.
Oak: one search summary of a merchant page said about 75% new oak. Ridge's tech sheet says 50% new. Ridge used, merchant page not read.
